# Pins are the exact versions installed and exercised in this environment
# (Windows 11, Python 3.11.9, CPU-only measurement runs). Generated by
# grepping actual `import`/`from` statements under ceq/, scale/, tests/,
# run_calib.py, then reading versions off the installed packages -- not
# from PyPI's latest or from memory. Re-derive with:
#   python -c "import torch,transformers,numpy,scipy; print(torch.__version__, transformers.__version__, numpy.__version__, scipy.__version__)"
#   pip show <pkg>
#
# transformers is pinned tight (== not >=). ceq/hf/modeling_ceq.py sets six
# private PreTrainedModel attributes (_supports_sdpa, _supports_flash_attn,
# _supports_flex_attn, _can_compile_fullgraph, _no_split_modules,
# _tied_weights_keys) that are undocumented HF internals, not public API --
# they can change shape or be renamed in any transformers release, including
# a patch release. The colab notebook's `transformers>=5.0` has no ceiling
# and can install a transformers that silently drops one of these overrides.
transformers==5.3.0

# torch: installed build is 2.5.1+cu121 (CUDA 12.1 wheel), but this repo's
# measurement loop is CPU-only (CUDA is owned by a separate process/nurse
# here, and tests/*/conftest.py already skip every CUDA-only test when
# torch.cuda.is_available() is False). The local version segment "+cu121" is
# only resolvable from https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu121, not plain
# PyPI, so pinning it verbatim would break `pip install -r requirements.txt`
# for anyone without that extra index. Pinning the bare version instead --
# installable as either the CPU or a matching CUDA wheel depending on the
# installer's index.
torch==2.5.1

numpy==1.26.4
scipy==1.17.1

# Used by tests/foreman/test_topology_washout.py as the ripser/persim
# reference oracle for persistent-homology diagrams.
ripser==0.6.14
persim==0.3.8

# ceq/hf/train.py: `from datasets import load_dataset` / `from
# huggingface_hub import HfApi`.
datasets==4.8.4
huggingface_hub==1.7.1

pytest==9.0.3

# triton: imported at module scope in ceq/mz_kernel.py and tests/chase/k22.py
# and tests/chase/conftest.py, but only exercised behind
# `requires_triton` (needs CUDA compute capability >= 8.0) -- so on a
# CPU-only machine the import still has to succeed, it just never runs a
# kernel. PyPI has no `triton` wheel for win32; on Windows it is shipped as
# the community fork `triton-windows`, which is what's installed here.
# On Linux/macOS a downloader needs `triton` instead -- version not pinned
# below because no such install was available here to read a real version
# off of; do not guess a number, verify it on that platform before pinning.
triton-windows==3.7.1.post27; sys_platform == "win32"
